### `Text`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Text = List Char
```

`command.ges` declares this too, and for the same reason: it is not
in the core prelude and a file that wants strings has to say so.


## The model


### `Value`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Value := Word | Number | Names | Range Int Int | AtLeast Int | OneOf (List Text) | Each (List Text)
```

What a column's value is drawn from — a `Value` below, one of the
five a single token can be: `Word`, `Number`, `Range lo hi`,
`AtLeast n`, `OneOf names` (`card:relational-model.md` Q2, the
domains Codd put in the schema).  `Names` and `Each` are no domain
of a column: a list is an `Of` with a rank.


### `Col`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Col := Col Text Value
```


### `Rel`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Rel := Rel Text (List Col) (List Text)
    Of Text Text (List Col) (List Text) Need
```

A relation: its name, its heading in order — **the key first**, so
a row reads as its identity and then its facts — and its key.
**An empty key means at most one row in a document.**

`Of parent field cols key need` is a relation keyed by its parent's
key, named `parent.field`: with no key of its own it holds at most
one row per parent — a value a record *may* carry, absent as no row
and never a null — and with a `rank` key it holds a list, one row a
name, the order a fact.  `need` says whether every parent must have
at least one row there — `Must` for a section's voices, `May` for a
note's manners — which is the one flag the model keeps, because it
is a rule about the model (an inclusion) and not about a line.


### `Line`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Line := Line Text Shape (List Text) (List Sort)
```

How one written line is laid out: its kind word, its shape, the
fields it folds in — a column of the relation named by the word, or
an `Of` of it — in the order they are written, and the order lines
of this kind are written in.  A `Headed` shape names the one token
written without a field name, and that name is not among the
fields; a `Bare` line's one field is.


## A value, and the line view


### `Need`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Need := Must | May
```

Whether a record of this kind has to carry the field.  The refusal a
missing one earns names it, so this is what makes that message
derivable rather than written twice.


### `Field`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Field := Field Text Value Need
```


## A kind


### `Shape`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Shape := Named | Bare Text | Headed Text
```

What the tokens after the kind word are.

`Named` — `key value key value …`, and nothing positional, which is
gate two of `spec/drawnscores.md`: *two fields of one shape telling
apart only by position* is the failure that made `manner`
unfindable.  `note` is this.

`Bare` — one value and no name, under the field name given.  `bpm 96`
is this, and so is every singleton line of a `.desk`.

`Headed` — one bare value first, then named fields.  `section A  key
D  bars 8` is this, and the bare one is the record's own name.


### `Sort`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Sort := By Text | Along Text Text Text | Among Text Text
```

How the lines of a kind are sorted when the file is written back.

`By` is the ordinary case: this field, ascending.

`Along` is the one the roll forced — the voice order is *the
section's own*, not alphabetical, because that is the order the roll
stacks them in (Henri, 2026-09-05).  So it names the field, the kind
that writes the order down, and that kind's field holding it.

`Among` is where a reference is ordered by **where the record it
names stands**: a note's `section` sorts by the section's place in
the file and not by its name, because a section is put where the
author put it.  Found 2026-09-09 by deriving the writer from this
declaration and noticing that `By "section"` agreed with the parser
only because `arc.notes` happens to name its sections A, B, C.


### `Kind`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Kind := Kind Text Shape (List Field) (List Text) (List Sort)
```

One kind of line, resolved: its word, the shape of its line, its
fields, the key of the relation it writes, and the order its lines
are written in — `lineKind` builds one from a `Line` and the model.

**An empty order means the order they were written in**, which is
what `section` has: a section list is the author's sequence and
sorting it would be a second thing to be canonical about.

## The line view, derived


### `lineKind`

```
lineKind rs l : List Rel -> Line -> Kind
```

**A `Kind` from a `Line` and the model** — the derivation `notes.py`
and the writer are held to.  Each field the line folds in is a
column of the line's relation (`Must`), or an `Of` of it: with no
key of its own a value the record may carry (`May`), with a rank a
list — `Each` its names when the value column is bounded, `Names`
otherwise — required or not as the `Of` says.
A field nothing owns yields no `Field` here and is refused by name
in the host (`facts.line_kind`), which reads the same model and
lines and is held to this.

```
lineField rs w f : List Rel -> Text -> Text -> List Field
```


```
valueDomain cs : List Col -> Value
```

The domain of an `Of`'s `value` column.

```
listValue d : Value -> Value
```

How a list reads on the line: each name from the list, or names.


## A type, as a value


### `Type`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Type := TyCon Text | TyApp Type Type | TyFun Type Type | TyInt Int | TyTuple (List Type)
```


### `fieldType`

```
fieldType f : Field -> Type
```

What a field's value is, as a type: a number is an `Int`, a word or
a bounded word a `Text`.  Names have no base column and no row type.


### `valueType`

```
valueType v : Value -> Type
```

A value's type: a number is an `Int`, a word or a bounded word a
`Text`, and so are names.


### `fieldScalar`

```
fieldScalar f : Field -> Bool
```

Whether a field is one token a row carries — everything but a list of
names, whose column is a relation of its own.


### `fieldNamed`

```
fieldNamed k n : Kind -> Text -> List Field
```

The field named `n`, if the kind has one.


### `kindColumns`

```
kindColumns k : Kind -> List Text
```

**The columns of a kind's base relation**, by name: the key, in key
order, then every required scalar field not in it, in declared
order.  This is the row `document` feeds and the fields a `Fact`
carries — `facts.base_columns` in the host, held equal to this by
`test/test_stage.py`.  A `Headed` kind's key names its bare first
token, which is no field of the record.


### `kindColumn`

```
kindColumn k f : Kind -> Field -> Bool
```


### `columnType`

```
columnType k n : Kind -> Text -> Type
```

A column's type: its field's, or a `Text` for a `Headed` kind's bare
name.


### `kindRow`

```
kindRow k : Kind -> Type
```

**The row of a kind, as a type**: a tuple of its columns' types — or
the one column's type, when there is one.


### `rowType`

```
rowType r : Rel -> Type
```

**The row of a relation, as a type**: a tuple of its heading's
types — or the one column's, when there is one.  `rowType` is for a
relation that stands alone; `relRow` reads an `Of`'s parent key off
the model.


### `relRow`

```
relRow rs r : List Rel -> Rel -> Type
```


### `documentRow`

```
documentRow rs name : List Rel -> Text -> List Type
```

The rows of the relation named `name` — what `document "name"` is
typed by, `document "section.voices"` included; an empty list is a
relation the program does not declare, and the compiler says so on
the author's line.
